source.title: Geometry-Lite: Interpretable Safety Probing via Layer-Wise Margin Geometry

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses a difference-in-means refusal-style probe as a baseline and evaluates prompt-level safety classification, but does not test refusal behavior or intervene on a refusal direction.
record.gate_note: The refusal-style probe measures classification of safe versus unsafe prompts, not whether the model refuses harmful requests or complies with harmless ones. Thus its scores do not test the claim versions. Results cited from other studies are not extracted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study uses the Arditi et al. difference-in-means construction only as a prompt-level safe/unsafe classification baseline (AUROC, TPR at fixed FPR). It reports no ablation, addition, weight edit, or refusal-rate measurement, so its results do not bear on whether the direction mediates refusal or on any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that prompt-level safety evidence lies mainly in persistent layer-wise margin position, not layer-to-layer drift, and that class-mean readouts transfer better under benchmark shift than optimized linear boundaries. They draw no conclusion about refusal mediation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates a difference-in-means refusal-style probe at the assistant-anchor position as a safety-classification baseline; it does not perform the original causal ablation or addition interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Readout geometry and evaluation distribution affect prompt-classification results; class-mean geometry is more stable on the hardest held-out benchmarks than optimized linear boundaries.

fits_no_version.finding: A refusal-style DIM projection at the assistant-anchor position separates safe from unsafe prompts with AUROC .863–.949 (avg .907) on the full test set and .794–.879 on the hard subset. This is below supervised multi-layer probes in all nine instruction-tuned models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A difference-in-means refusal-style readout carries prompt-harmfulness classification signal, weaker than supervised linear probes in-distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Class-mean (DIM/centroid) readouts keep more class separation under leave-one-benchmark-out shift (held-out/train ratio about 1.2 all-LOBO, 0.92–0.95 hard-LOBO) than optimized linear boundaries (0.43, 0.31).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Difference-in-means harmfulness readouts are more stable under benchmark shift than optimized linear probes.

record.problems: The refusal-style probe results are classification metrics rather than measures of refusal behavior; no causal intervention on the direction is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Other probe and multi-layer baseline results were left out because they are not the refusal-style difference-in-means readout and do not measure refusal behavior.

untested.parts: Ablation removing refusal, addition inducing refusal, preservation of other abilities; no refusal behaviour measured.
Weight-edit (abliteration) removal of refusal in released models.
Whether jailbreaks suppress the direction; adversarial training against ablation. WildJailbreak/JBB prompts are only classification data.
Whether refusal is affine, a cone, or multi-directional. Multi-layer DIM stacking is a classifier, not a test of refusal dimensionality.
Separation of harmfulness encoding from the refusal decision. The probes read prompt harmfulness labels only, with no refusal outcome.
Transfer across languages, variants, or base-to-instruct. LOBO is benchmark shift for a classifier, not direction transfer.
Effect of refusal training on direction existence.
Reasoning models. Qwen3 is used, but no refusal intervention is tested and thinking mode is not addressed.

missing.what: Refusal-style probe AUROC and TPR@1/3/5% FPR on the static-probe uncertainty slice (avg AUROC .741). This is classification only and does not bear on any version.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are classification baselines, correctly linked to none with state cannot_determine. The refusal-style probe is the authors' comparator, not the study's own method. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Ablation, addition, refusal behavior, and preservation of other abilities.
Weight-edit removal of refusal in released models.
Whether attacks suppress the direction or training against ablation improves robustness.
Whether refusal is carried by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
Whether harmfulness judgment and refusal decision are separately encoded.
Transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or training stages.
How refusal training determines whether a removable direction exists.
Whether the claim holds for reasoning models.
